$comment: THE CLASSIFIER CORPUS. Read by BOTH implementations — src/php/Core and, later, src/phorj/core.
This file is the ground truth for the tenure classifier and is listed in CLAUDE.md § Credentials & stateful data as
stateful data that must not be casually removed or relabelled. CLAUDE.md: 'Never weaken a
classifier test to make a change pass. If a fixture goes red, the classifier regressed.'
PROVENANCE IS HONEST AND MACHINE-CHECKED. spec/PROJECT_BRIEF.md §4 asks for >=30 *real* listing
texts. Real texts cannot be captured until a source endpoint or a browser session exists (blocked
on U3 — the DevTools cURL captures). So every entry declares provenance: 'synthetic' texts are
hand-written French listing prose modelled on how these landlords actually word their pages;
'captured' entries are frozen from a real payload and scrubbed. The suite asserts the declared
synthetic/captured counts match reality, so the gap stays visible as data rather than as a comment.
id           stable identifier; never renumber, only append
source       the SourceProfile this listing arrived from
expect.tenure / expect.outcome   the hand label — the thing under test
why          why a human labelled it that way; the record for a future relabelling argument

icf_novedis.name: icf_novedis
icf_novedis.$why: FLIPPED to true on 2026-08-06 after review. CLAUDE.md's reviewer charter names ICF among the landlords that publish social AND intermediate stock. Novedis is genuinely ICF Habitat's non-social arm, so `false` is defensible for a Novedis-only endpoint and wrong for the group portal — and nothing in this repo yet says which the adapter will target, because config/rent/sources.json does not exist. mixed_tenure is the single flag that disarms the fail-closed rule, so it takes the safe value until that is decided. Tracked as an open question.

example_pure_lli.$comment: SYNTHETIC, and deliberately not a real landlord. Until 2026-08-23 In'li carried this shape, and hydration disproved it: the source publishes PLS stock its cards never mention. No LIVE source is pure-LLI today. The classifier still SUPPORTS the shape -- a source with no social stock has nothing to confuse a thin signal with, so `mixed_tenure: false` lets it MATCH below the floor -- and spec/PROJECT_BRIEF.md §11 requires the shape to be covered. Leaning that coverage on a real source is what let a false premise sit in the corpus for weeks, so it is a fixture now. It is absent from config/rent/sources.json on purpose; testEveryCorpusSourceAgreesWithConfig skips sources it cannot find there.

cases.title: T4 CROISSY-SUR-SEINE - 3 CHAMBRES, PLUS UN BUREAU
cases.description: TROIS CHAMBRES, PLUS UN BUREAU FERME ET UNE BUANDERIE.
cases.why: RELABELLED 2026-08-07 after review round 6, evidence here and in the commit message as CLAUDE.md requires. Round 6 found the round-5 doubt floor was scoped to structured FIELDS only, so the identical fail-open was still live in prose: 'Logements finances en PLUS' reached MATCH at confidence 50 on In'li, while the same sentence with PLS rejected. Extending the floor to prose is what closes it -- and this fixture is the one case in the corpus that pays for it. A SHOUTED 'PLUS' that no comparative explains is now a doubt wherever it appears, so this all-caps title digests instead of matching. That is the accepted cost, and it is the small side of the trade: one glance in the digest for a listing whose title happens to shout, against a wasted application for a social listing that reads as ordinary French. ORIGINAL LABEL, for the record: LIBRE / MATCH / max_confidence 59. Its ORIGINAL RATIONALE still holds and is why the fixture is kept rather than deleted: FOUND BY SABOTAGE-CHECK, 2026-08-06, and it took two attempts to write correctly. Every other 'plus' trap here is followed by a comparative ('plus de', 'plus tard', 'plus lumineux'), so the comparative suppression alone caught all of them and the collocation test could be deleted with the suite staying green. This one has no comparative to fall back on — 'PLUS' is followed by 'UN'. It must also be SHOUTED: uppercase is enforced by the acronym pattern itself, so a lowercase 'plus' never reaches the collocation test at all, and a lowercase version of this fixture proves nothing. An all-caps portal title with 'PLUS UN BUREAU' is ordinary, and only the collocation test stands between it and a social-housing classification.

cases.title: Logement conventionné
cases.description: Logement libre au 1er août 2026. T3 de 65 m².
cases.why: P0 REGRESSION GUARD (review, 2026-08-06), and the worst defect found in this module. 'logement libre' was in the label table as tenure LIBRE; it is not a tenure term at all but the standard French VACANCY phrase. It fired tier 2 at 90 on a move-in date, and the spurious LIBRE then satisfied the conventionné exception — which tested isEligible() rather than 'is an intermediate label'. Result: a listing whose own TITLE reads 'Logement conventionné' reached MATCH, with the word absent from its reasons. A §1 breach via two independently reasonable-looking table entries.

cases.title: T3 Herblay
cases.description: Logement conventionne, loyer plafonne.
cases.why: RELABELLED 2026-08-06 after review round 4, with the evidence here and in the commit message as CLAUDE.md requires. Round 3 made a tier-1 LLI field qualify a 'conventionne' ANYWHERE in the text, on the ladder argument that a structured field is the strongest evidence there is. Round 4 showed what that buys: a description reading '40 logements conventionnes reserves aux menages sous plafond de ressources, et 12 logements en location' MATCHED on the strength of one field, with the word 'conventionne' absent from reasons[]. The exemption was removed outright rather than bounded again -- two attempts at bounding it both leaked, and every leak was in the notify direction. The listing now digests, and its reasons[] name the 'conventionne' explicitly, so a human sees exactly what the classifier saw. A genuine LLI whose text also says 'conventionne' costs one glance; the alternative costs an application. ORIGINAL LABEL, for the record: LLI / MATCH / min_confidence 90, added in round 3 because the conventionne exception looked at tier-2 labels only, so LLI declared through a STRUCTURED FIELD — the strongest evidence the ladder has — did not count as 'explicitly labelled intermediate', while the weaker text label did. Genuine LLI stock digested when its evidence arrived through the best channel. Fail-closed, so not a breach, but inconsistent with the ladder it claims to implement.

cases.title: T2 Domont
cases.description: Logement conventionne, loyer libre.
cases.why: THE EXCEPTION IS FOR INTERMEDIATE LABELS ONLY, and this is the fixture that says so. CLAUDE.md's glossary excuses conventionne when the listing is 'explicitly labelled intermediate' — LIBRE is not intermediate, it is market rate, so a LIBRE label must NOT disarm the exclusion. Without this case the drop-rule could be widened from '=== LLI' back to 'isEligible()' with the suite staying green, which is exactly how the P0 of 2026-08-06 was built: a spurious LIBRE signal satisfied the exception and a conventionne listing reached MATCH. The two labels here genuinely contradict each other (subsidised vs market rate), so withholding is also the honest reading.

cases.title: LOGEMENT PLUS MODERNE - T3 CHATOU
cases.description: BIEN RENOVE, PROCHE COMMERCES.
cases.why: Found by review 2026-08-06. The collocation guard suppressed adverbial PLUS via a denylist of French adjectives, so any adjective NOT on the list — moderne, confortable, economique, agreable, ensoleille — turned an emphatic title into tenure PLUS and a silent REJECT. A denylist of French adjectives cannot be completed. The guard now asks the closed question instead: does a financing label END the phrase (punctuation, end of text, another acronym)? If a word follows and it is a known comparative, it was the adverb; if a word follows and it is anything else, it is genuinely indecidable and lands here — visible in the digest rather than silently dropped OR silently matched.

cases.title: T3 - LLI
cases.description: Un numéro unique d'enregistrement est exigé pour toute demande.
cases.why: Found by review 2026-08-06. The fold tables carry PRECOMPOSED accented codepoints only, so text arriving NFD-decomposed ('e' + U+0301) was not folded and 'numéro unique d'enregistrement' never matched its literal — while the unaccented 'LLI' in the same listing still did. The social side vanished and the eligible side survived, which is the wrong direction to fail in. Combining marks are now stripped after the table: one line, locale-free, and portable to phorj. NOTE: this fixture's description is deliberately written with \u0301 escapes; do not 'tidy' it into precomposed characters, or it stops testing anything.

cases.title: T3 Taverny
cases.description: Appartement 3 pieces.
cases.why: Found by review 2026-08-06. Two structured fields each match at offset 0 of their own value, so the tie-break decides. resolve()'s comparator had its two strlen terms transposed, making the SHORTER evidence win — the opposite of its own docblock — so 'lli' (3) beat 'plai' (4) and an explicit PLAI field landed in the user-visible digest instead of REJECT. A phorj port written from the docblock would have disagreed with the PHP on exactly this input, which is the differential the shared corpus exists to expose.

cases.title: T3 en résidence conventionnée
cases.description: Appartement 3 pieces, proche gare.
cases.why: P0 REGRESSION GUARD (review round 2, 2026-08-06). FRENCH INFLECTION. Every literal was matched exactly with a trailing word-boundary guard, so 'conventionnée' -- the feminine agreement, which is what you write before 'résidence' -- was a NON-MATCH while 'conventionné' matched. On In'li (a pure source) that meant LLI/MATCH at 50 instead of CONVENTIONNE/REJECT. The acronyms (PLAI, ANRU, ANAH, HLM) are invariant, which is exactly why the table read as safe: the terms a reviewer checks first are the ones that could not break. Compare conv-001 and conv-002, which test the ACCENT but not the agreement.

cases.title: Résidence mixte - Cergy
cases.description: Résidence mixte de logements sociaux et intermédiaires. Loyer intermédiaire à partir de 900 euros.
cases.why: P0 REGRESSION GUARD (review round 2, 2026-08-06), and the worst of the inflection class. The listing's own description says 'logements sociaux'. Because the plural did not match, NO excluded signal existed at all — so the conflict rule had nothing to see, and 'loyer intermédiaire' carried this to LLI/MATCH at full tier-2 confidence. It was notified. With inflection the social label fires at an earlier position than the intermediate one, wins the tier, and the documented asymmetry applies: an excluded verdict is never softened by a contradicting eligible signal, so this REJECTs rather than digesting. That is the intended reading of a mixed résidence — the specific unit is unproven and the cost of being wrong is a wasted application. (I predicted DIGEST when writing this fixture; the code was right and the prediction was wrong.)

False: inflectedTokenPosition joins a literal's words with '\s*', which matches a newline, and only ELIGIBLE tells were blocked from spanning. Once the classifier began reading every field, Text::fold()'s entity gate ran on URLs and surface cells -- and '&' in an href is the ordinary output of an HTML scrape, so one link turned the whole listing into UNKNOWN/DIGEST. It also SOFTENED determinate rejections: a description naming PLAI went from REJECT to DIGEST because an unrelated field was encoded, which the class doctrine forbids outright. Incidental surfaces now use Text::foldTolerant(), which substitutes a space for an entity rather than refusing -- the one repair that can neither invent a match nor hide one, since every literal is matched with '\\s*' between its words. Detection survives: see regress-046.

An entity sitting inside a multi-word label is exactly the asymmetric failure Text::INVISIBLE exists for -- it deletes that label and leaves every other one standing. Replacing it with a space keeps the label matchable, because inflectedTokenPosition joins a literal's words with '\\s*'. Deleting it instead would make this listing silent, which is the §1 fail-open wearing a repair as a disguise.

cases.title: T3 Le Vesinet
cases.description: Bel appartement lumineux.

An incidental surface is DECODED, not space-substituted: '­' decodes to U+00AD, which Text::INVISIBLE strips, so 'plai­sir' becomes 'plaisir' and correctly matches nothing. The first implementation substituted a space, which produced 'plai sir' and invented a token inside *plaisir* -- the silent drop Text::hasToken() exists to prevent, reintroduced through the repair. It also matters WHERE the split happens: splitting an identifier on non-alphanumerics before invisibles are stripped puts the boundary back, so the split runs on the invisible-stripped form. See regress-047 for the same fold in the §1 direction.

Decoding has neither failure mode, because the machinery that already exists handles the result: the decoded character is stripped by INVISIBLE and the token is restored.

cases.title: Appartement 3  pièces 62 m²
cases.description: Aménagement Duplex Loft Plain-pied Triplex Prestations Balcon / Loggia Terrasse Jardin Cave Garage/Box Parking Cellier Accessibilité Ascenseur Logement adapté Chauffage Individuel Collectif Pour ajouter plusieurs annonces au comparateur, veuillez d'abord retirer une ou plusieurs annonces.
cases.why: THE HARD ONE, and the FIFTH outing of this project's most expensive failure class: excluded vocabulary appearing as ordinary French, or as UI furniture, on a page that is not about tenure. This text is verbatim from Logirep's own search-filter strip and it contains THREE of them -- PLAI inside 'Plain-pied', LLI inside 'Cellier', PLUS inside 'plusieurs'. None is a tenure signal, and a classifier that read any of them would reject or mislabel every listing on the source while SourceHealth stayed green and the item count stayed plausible, which is hard rule 2's silent failure arriving through the classifier rather than the parser. It is captured as a DESCRIPTION on purpose: the previous four instances (CDC's 'au plus pres', Cityloger's 'bailleur social', Erilia's 'Ai-je droit a un logement social ?') all turned on WHICH SURFACE the text reached, and a selector widened to a page-level container is exactly how this strip would get in. The guards already hold -- every string here was run through TenureClassifier on 2026-08-21 and returned UNKNOWN at 0.00 -- so this fixture exists to keep them holding, not to fix anything. Note the facet case differs from the four before it: those were prose written by a human about a flat; this is a FILTER LABEL, which no amount of care in writing listing copy would ever remove.

cases.title: Appartement de 63 m² à LES ULIS
cases.description: Exclusivité - appartement 3 pièces de 63.0 m² aux Ulis Sans frais d'agence. L'espace de vie comprend un salon et une cuisine. Présence d'un gardien. Le bien est situé au 3e étage. Chauffage collectif. Une place de parking incluse. Proximité de bus et de lignes de RER B et C avec plusieurs stations accessibles. Commerces à proximité.
cases.why:
THE FURNITURE CLASS ON A FOURTH SOURCE, and the first time it arrives on a source that is NOT mixed-tenure. Captured from In'li's /location-appartement-les-ulis-91940/PRV-054595 on 2026-08-23, the day In'li gained a detail_map: its cards carry four facts and no title, so `exclude_title_patterns` was structurally dead on the source producing two thirds of the matches.

The trap is `plusieurs stations`. `plus` is one of the commonest words in French and it is also the excluded financing acronym PLUS, and reading the second where the first was written has now cost this repo four instances: CDC's `au plus près` (which vetoed 14 of 16 correctly-badged listings into the digest), Cityloger's `bailleur social`, Logirep's `Ce·lli·er` inside a filter facet, and this.

WHAT MAKES THIS ONE DIFFERENT, and why it is worth a case of its own: In'li is `mixed_tenure: false`, so a listing with no tenure signal is notified on the source default. Every earlier instance of this class cost a listing its MATCH by pushing it to the digest — fail-closed, wasteful, safe. Here a false PLUS would be an outright REJECT of a listing on a pure-LLI landlord's own site, and the yield would simply drop with nothing to see. Adding a description to a source that previously had almost none is exactly the change that could introduce it, which is why this case was captured on the same day that change landed.

The expectation is the verdict the BARE CARD already gets: LLI on the source default. The description must not alter it in either direction — a veto would reject good stock, and a promotion would mean prose was doing work the source default is already doing at a deliberately sub-threshold confidence.

cases.title: Appartement 3 pièces
cases.description: Logement soumis à plafond de ressources : 26 920 € de revenu fiscal de référence pour une personne seule.
cases.why: TIER 4, THE ONLY DIRECTION THE REAL FIGURES SUPPORT. 26 920 EUR is the 2026 PLUS ceiling for one person, and it sits strictly below 36 144 EUR -- the LOWEST intermediate ceiling anywhere in Ile-de-France (zone B1, one person, BOFiP BOI-BAREME-000017). A figure below that cannot be an intermediate ceiling whatever the household size or zone, so the financing is social. This is the whole of tier 4: below the boundary it concludes, above it says nothing.

cases.title: Appartement 3 pièces
cases.description: Plafond de ressources : 44 344 € pour une personne seule. Résidence récente, proche RER.
cases.why: THE FALSE POSITIVE TIER 4 EXISTS TO AVOID. 44 344 EUR is the INTERMEDIATE ceiling for one person in zones A bis and A -- an eligible listing quoting its own ceiling. It sits inside the measured overlap (36 144 .. 109 595 EUR), where a figure could belong to either regime, so tier 4 must stay silent and let the listing fall through to the digest on its own thin evidence. Firing here would reject a real match on the strength of a number that proves the opposite.

cases.title: Appartement 3 pièces
cases.description: Bel appartement lumineux, loyer plafonné à 1 250 € charges comprises, résidence 2021.
cases.why: LOAD-BEARING, and it is the same lesson twice. This classifier's vocabulary note already records that `loyer plafonne` is THE PRIMARY TARGET DESCRIBING ITSELF -- intermediate housing is by definition capped rent -- and adding it as a doubt once digested lli-004, lli-011 and regress-030. The numeric tier can recreate that defect a second way: an extractor anchored on a bare `plafond` reads 1 250 EUR as an income ceiling, which is below every threshold, and concludes SOCIAL. On a pure-LLI source the contrast is at its sharpest -- this listing MATCHES today, and one careless anchor turns it into a REJECT. So the anchor is `plafond de ressources` and nothing else. Paired with lli-008, which is this listing without the rent-cap phrase.

cases.title: Appartement 3 pièces
cases.description: Location libre, sans plafond de ressources : revenu minimum exigé 30 000 € par an. Dossier simplifié, disponible immédiatement.
cases.why: A SIGNAL MANUFACTURED FROM ITS OWN NEGATION, which is hard rule 9 read one more way. `sans plafond de ressources` advertises the ABSENCE of a ceiling and is ordinary private-market copy. THE FIGURE IS THE POINT: 30 000 EUR is an income FLOOR an agency demands of a tenant, and it sits below the 36 144 EUR threshold -- so a reader that skipped the negation would conclude SOCIAL and reject a private-market flat. The first version of this case carried no number at all, so the guard it claims to pin was never reached and a sabotage run showed the negation branch could be deleted with the suite staying green. Same rule as Prose's lift reader: read the negation before the fact.

cases.title: Appartement 3 pièces
cases.description: Logement intermédiaire. Plafond de loyer annuel : 15 000 € charges comprises. Résidence 2023.
cases.why: WHAT THE ANCHOR UNIQUELY PROTECTS, and it took a sabotage run to find a case that shows it. The obvious example -- `loyer plafonne a 1 250 EUR` -- is guarded twice over and so proves nothing: folded, `plafonne` is not `plafond`, and 1 250 is below the plausibility floor anyway. This one defeats both of those. `Plafond de loyer` is a real intermediate concept quoted as a real ANNUAL figure, so the number is plausible and the word is `plafond` exactly. Only the `de ressources` half of the anchor keeps a RENT ceiling from being read as an INCOME ceiling -- and 15 000 EUR sits below the 36 144 EUR threshold, so a loosened anchor concludes SOCIAL, contradicts this listing's own explicit intermediate label, and digests a flat the tool exists to find.
